Perfect! After Bxd3+ Qc2, Black still has Bxc2# (mate)! So Bxd3+ is forcing checkmate in all variations. This is the move!

**Best move:** Bxd3+

**Main line:** Bxd3+ Qxd3 Qb2#

**Motif:** fork (the bishop forks king and queen on d3, and all defensive tries lead to mate)

**Explanation (for the coaching note):**

The club player should spot that White's d3 pawn is pinned to the king on b1 (it can't move because it's defending the king from the bishop on a3). When a piece is pinned, it becomes a prime target because it can't escape. By playing Bxd3+, Black removes the defender and forces White's hand—all three defensive tries (Qxd3, Rxd3, or Qc2) allow immediate checkmate with either Qb2# or Qc1#. Always look for pinned pieces and consider sacrificing or attacking them when they're trapped.
